title: Why Japanese Businesses Are Investing in India
paragraphs: Japanese companies are increasingly turning to India, and the number of Japanese businesses operating in the country has reached a record high.

According to a report by the consulting firm Grant Thornton Bharat, there were 1,463 Japanese-owned businesses in India in 2026, up from 1,374 the year before. These companies employ more than 459,000 people. Japanese investment in India has also grown significantly. In the 2025-26 financial year, Japanese foreign direct investment in India reached $3.75 billion, bringing the total to more than $48 billion.

So why are Japanese companies so interested in India? One major reason is the country's size and potential. India has a huge population, a large pool of skilled workers and a fast-growing economy. These strengths complement Japan's long-term capital, advanced technology and manufacturing expertise.

In addition, India has become a popular choice for Japanese firms looking to expand overseas. In a survey by the Japan Bank for International Cooperation, India was ranked the most promising destination for overseas business for several years in a row.
Supply chains are another factor. Some Japanese companies are looking to reduce their dependence on China, and India offers an alternative.

The types of investment are also changing. In the past, Japanese companies in India focused mainly on manufacturing. Today, they are also investing in areas such as technology, finance and research. Key areas of cooperation now include semiconductors, artificial intelligence, clean energy and critical minerals. For example, the carmaker Suzuki is investing in a new plant and research facilities, while the air conditioner maker Daikin is building a research and development center.

Governments are also supporting the trend. Japan has set a goal of investing 10 trillion yen in India over the next decade, and leaders from the two countries signed many new agreements at a summit in July 2026.
According to Grant Thornton, India is becoming a center for innovation within the global operations of Japanese companies, not just a place to manufacture goods.
